old_content._doc: SpecLFB: first speculative load left unprotected (UV6).
old_content.note: UV6 = first spec load in LSQ performs its in-window cache access

_superseded_note.why: the old file described one bug (UV6), not a criterion; UV6 is now one case the criterion below catches (the implementation's isUnsafe flag is wrong, the paper's definition is used)

_doc: SpecLFB transmission criterion: an unsafe speculative load's miss may not refill (fill, and evict a victim from) L1D or L2; parking in the LFB is allowed. O3PipeView trace only (SimSpect hooks). Evaluated by STAGE3_gem5/check_footprint.py. Scope quotes re-checked against wiki/findings/mdsToRead/FOOTPRINT_DEFENSES_PAPER_AUDIT.md §3, §7 and the PDF text (printed pages = PDF page + 629).

requires.why: the gem5 implementation protects both cache levels; STT_6_speclfb ran without L2 (audit finding 2), so only L1D was observable there

claims.quote: [the LFB check prevents] potentially unsafe speculative loads from being reloaded from lower-level cache into adjacent upper-level cache (e.g. from L2 cache into L1 data cache (L1D cache)) … both cache levels of X86 O3 CPU model in Gem5
SpecLFB is applied to both levels of the cache in the O3 CPU model in Gem5.
eliminating cache side channels in speculative execution established by flush- and conflict-based cache side-channel attacks, which require pre-evicting the cache lines to be leaked.
claims.supports: observation.state = presence (fills + the victim evictions they cause)

claims.quote: the speculative loads causing cache misses are considered unsafe and should be protected.
claims.supports: actors: misses only; hits leave no fill event

claims.quote: Only when the security check mechanism determines that it is safe, can the data be refilled into the L1D cache.
MUSL = an unsafe speculative load that causes cache miss; control-flow MUSLs are safe if there are no older control instructions that are unresolved (p638)
claims.supports: actors.modes.spec (pinned; the control-flow part equals STT_6)

observation.notes: Classic caches: no coh events exist (SIMSPECT_HOOKS.md), and coherence is not claimed. repl_touch is excluded: replacement metadata is out of scope (below). spec is the paper's definition, not SpecLFB's isUnsafe flag; UV6 is that flag being wrong.

spec.text: squashed(i) ∧ lc_seq < i.seq  (pinned 2026-10-28: what the tests realize; i = the event's seq joined to the O3PipeView fetch seqNum; squashed = never retired and younger than a ROB:squash seq while allocated before that squash)

footprint.text: lc_retire < e.tick < fnc_retire (fnc_retire==0 → ∞; no lc annotated → no lower bound) ∧ every annotated unresolved branch still unresolved at e.tick (gem5_common.check_branch_resolutions), same window as check_ld.py

leak.text: leak ⇔ ∃ e ∈ E({fill, evict}, {L1D, L2}) : actor(e.seq) ∧ e ∈ W  (LFB buf_fill/buf_release allowed)

not_covered.item: LFB path never exercised at runtime
not_covered.why: SIMSPECT_HOOKS.md: on every verification gadget SpecLFB classified the spec loads isUnsafe=0, so LFB hooks are compiled but untested; a no-leak verdict via LFB parking is unverified until a gadget exercises it
paper's unsafe sources are broader than control flow (§5 p635-638); the pinned actor (STT_6 tests) realizes control-flow speculation only

out_of_scope.item: speculative cache hits and replacement (LRU) metadata
out_of_scope.note: scoping problem of the defense, not an implementation bug we catch

claim.quote: Leakage through speculative loads under cache hits is out of the current defense scope of SpecLFB. … because LFB cannot intercept the data loaded by speculative instructions under cache hits, it does not prevent speculative changes to cache metadata.

out_of_scope.item: TLB, port contention and other speculative side channels (incl. L1I, not claimed)
out_of_scope.note: scoping problem of the defense, not an implementation bug we catch

claim.quote: We do not consider other speculative side channels, such as TLB [20], port contention [4,7], etc.

out_of_scope.note: not implemented in gem5, so not testable here (an implementation gap of the defense, not a bug we catch)

claim.quote: Remark: To the best of our knowledge, both Gem5 and SonicBOOM at their current versions where we implement SpecLFB do not support VP.
